The claim is mathematically correct. For a deterministic one-pass machine, each prefix p reaches exactly one state q_p. The matrix U has exactly one 1 per row (at column q_p). Matrix V has rows indexed by states, with V[q,r] = 1 iff suffix r is accepted starting from state q. Then (UV)[p,r] = sum_q U[p,q]V[q,r] = U[p,q_p]V[q_p,r] = V[q_p,r] = M[p,r]. This equality holds as integer matrices, hence over any field. Rank bound: rank(UV) <= min(rank(U), rank(V)) <= number of columns of U = |Q_reached| <= |Q| = 2^S. No counterexample exists; this is a standard fact in automata theory and communication complexity (the rank of the communication matrix of a deterministic protocol is at most the number of states reached).

The circuit composition claim is mathematically correct. Given circuits for psi (size A), psi^{-1} on valid codes C (size B), and delta_a (size T), their composition psi ∘ delta_a ∘ psi^{-1} on valid codes has a circuit of size at most A+B+T plus constant wiring. This is a standard circuit composition fact. The caveat is also correct: A and B may be large (the encoding/decoding circuits themselves may be complex), so this does not give a recoding-invariant lower bound on the intrinsic complexity of the transition function, and it does not close G0001 which requires a bound independent of the encoding choice.

proved_step: RESIDUAL QUOTIENT LEMMA (exact statement and proof). Let A and B be sets, let F:A*→B, and define u~v iff for every w∈A*, F(uw)=F(vw). Then ~ is an equivalence relation, is stable under appending a letter, and its classes form the coarsest reachable-state deterministic transducer computing F, with output [u]↦F(u) when outputs are read after each complete input. Proof: Reflexivity, symmetry and transitivity follow pointwise from equality in B. If u~v and a∈A, then for every w, F(uaw)=F(vaw), since aw∈A*; hence ua~va, so δ([u],a)=[ua] is well-defined. Define output λ([u])=F(u), which is well-defined by choosing suffix ε in the definition. Starting from [ε], induction on input length shows that the state after u is [u], hence the output is F(u). For coarseness, any deterministic transducer computing F that reaches the same state after u and v must produce the same output after every common suffix w, so F(uw)=F(vw) for all w; thus u~v. This is a general mathematical lemma about exact deterministic transducers. It supplies no bound on Boolean update-circuit size, update time, decoder complexity, or simulation of the MMW Sigma3SAT^A oracle, and does not close G0001.

statement: For every Boolean oracle A:{0,1}^q->{0,1}, one query A(z) can be implemented by an ordinary Boolean circuit of O(2^q) gates; replacing t oracle gates costs O(t 2^q) gates.
proof: Build a depth-q binary decision tree querying the input bits, with 2^q leaves labeled by A's truth table. Each internal node is a 2-to-1 mux, so the tree has 2^q-1 muxes and returns A(z) on every input. Replacing each of t oracle gates independently gives O(t 2^q) gates. The circuit description uses A's truth table; no uniform polynomial-time construction from an arbitrary oracle is asserted.

statement: Let an oracle circuit C have g ordinary Boolean gates and oracle gates A_1,...,A_t. Suppose oracle gate i computes a fixed Boolean function A_i:{0,1}^{q_i}->{0,1} that has an ordinary Boolean circuit of size a_i. Then C has an oracle-free Boolean circuit computing the same function with at most g+sum_{i=1}^t a_i gates (up to a fixed constant for wiring), by replacing each oracle gate by its circuit and connecting its q_i inputs to the former query wires. If a uniform compiler constructs each replacement in time polynomial in q_i and a_i, the whole replacement description is constructible in time polynomial in g+sum_i(q_i+a_i). This is conditional: it gives no bound on a_i for Sigma_3SAT^A query predicates.
proof: Replace each oracle gate A_i by its circuit, preserving the gate's input and output wires. Each replacement computes the same function on every query input. Induction over the topological order of C shows that every wire value, including the output, is preserved. The gate counts add to g+sum_i a_i. Under the stated compiler condition, constructing and wiring all replacements takes polynomial time in the total listed size.

statement: For every sufficiently large q and every fixed finite basis of fan-in-two Boolean gates, some Boolean function A:{0,1}^q->{0,1} requires Omega(2^q/q) gates over that basis.
proof: There are 2^(2^q) Boolean functions on q bits. For a fixed finite basis, the number of circuits with at most g gates is at most (q+g)^(C g) for a basis-dependent constant C, by encoding each gate's type and at most two earlier wires and then the output wire. Set g=floor(2^q/(Dq)) for a sufficiently large constant D. For all sufficiently large q, (q+g)^(C g)<2^(2^q), so some Boolean function is not computed by any circuit of at most g gates. This gives the claimed lower bound.

statement: Let an oracle update circuit have at most g ordinary fan-in-two gates and t oracle gates. Suppose every oracle gate computes a fixed Boolean function on at most Q input bits. There is an oracle-free fan-in-two circuit for the same update with at most g + 3t(2^Q-1) gates, up to constant wiring overhead. In particular, if g,t are polynomial in s and Q <= a log_2(s) for a fixed constant a, the resulting circuit has polynomial size in s. Proof: For each oracle function on q<=Q bits, construct its complete binary decision tree. Each internal node is a 2-to-1 mux, implementable with a constant number (at most three) of fan-in-two Boolean gates, so the tree uses at most 3(2^q-1) gates and computes the truth-table function on every input. Replace each oracle gate by its tree, connecting the original query wires to the tree inputs. In topological order, every replacement returns the same answer as the oracle gate; induction over the original circuit's gate order shows every subsequent wire and the output are unchanged. Summing the costs gives the bound. If Q<=a log_2(s), then 2^Q<=s^a, and polynomial g,t imply polynomial total size. This is only a size statement; uniform construction still requires access to each truth table or an appropriate uniform compiler.

evidence: Binary decision tree construction is correct: a depth-q binary decision tree has 2^q leaves, 2^q-1 internal nodes. Each internal node is a 2-to-1 multiplexer (MUX). Replacing t oracle gates independently gives O(t 2^q). The statement correctly notes no uniform construction from arbitrary oracle is asserted. This is a standard and correct construction.

statement_start: LEMMA (Formal Oracle Query Length Barrier for Transfer T0). Let M be the MMW19 one-pass streaming algorithm for Search-MCSP[s] with a Sigma3SAT^A oracle (Thm 1.2). Its oracle queries have length q = O~(s). Proof: (1) MMW19 gives q = O~(s). (2) The oracle computes f_A: {0,1}^q -> {0,1} where f_A is Sigma3SAT^A. For random A, f_A is a random function. (5) Any poly(s)-size simulation would contradict Shannon. (6) Transfer T0 requires poly(s) simulation to apply Theorem 4.1 (streaming-to-circuit connection). (7) Since 2^Omega(s) is not poly(s), the simulation premise fails. Therefore T0 does not exclude the MMW19 oracle algorithm; the oracle gates break the poly(s) simulation premise exactly at the query length q = O~(s).

statement: Lemma (truth-table compilation upper bound). For any Boolean function h:{0,1}^q->{0,1}, a circuit with g oracle gates querying h on q-bit inputs can be replaced by an equivalent fan-in-2 Boolean circuit of size O(g q 2^q). Proof: Express h as the OR of conjunctions specifying each accepting q-bit string. Each conjunction needs at most q-1 AND gates; at most 2^q such terms need at most 2^q-1 OR gates. The empty accepting set is constant 0. Replace each oracle gate independently and sum the gate counts. This is an upper bound only; it gives no matching lower bound for a particular h and does not by itself yield a uniform resource-preserving streaming simulation.
evidence: The DNF construction works for every h and q>=1.

statement: Conditional compilation lemma. Let s>=2. Suppose each streaming update makes at most s^a oracle queries, each query has length q(s)<=b log_2 s, and the queried Boolean function is fixed for that input length. Replacing each oracle query by its full truth-table DNF yields an oracle-free fan-in-2 circuit for the update of size O(s^a q(s) 2^{q(s)} + C(s)), where C(s) is the size of the non-oracle update computation. In particular this is polynomial in s whenever C(s) is polynomial in s. Proof: for a query of q bits, encode each accepting input by a conjunction of its q literals, then OR the terms; shared input negations and binary fan-in give O(q 2^q) gates, including the constant-function cases. Substitute this circuit at each query gate, sum over at most s^a queries, and retain the original C(s) non-oracle gates. Since 2^{q(s)}<=s^b and q(s)<=b log s, the added size is O(s^{a+b} log s). This is a conditional upper bound, not a claim that MMW19 meets q=O(log s).

proved_step: statement: Residual-function compiler. For a Boolean function h on q ordered input bits, let W be the total number of distinct nonconstant residual functions at levels 0 through q-1, where a residual is obtained by fixing a prefix of the ordered bits. Then h has a fan-in-2 circuit with at most 3W+q gates, allowing constant terminals at no cost. Proof: At each level make one node for each distinct residual. For a residual r at level i, its restrictions r0 and r1 after fixing bit i+1 are either constants or residuals represented at level i+1. Compute r as (not x_{i+1} AND r0) OR (x_{i+1} AND r1), using at most three fan-in-2 gates and one shared negation per input bit. At level q all residuals are constants, so no further nodes are needed. Induction upward shows each node computes its named residual, including h at the root. statement: Bounded residual-width compilation. Let h:{0,1}^q->{0,1} have a fixed variable order. Suppose that at every prefix length i in {0,...,q-1}, the set of distinct nonconstant residual functions obtained by fixing the first i variables has size at most w. Then h has a fan-in-2 Boolean circuit of size at most 3qw+q, with free constant terminals. Proof: At each level i create one circuit node per distinct nonconstant residual at that level. For each such residual r, its two restrictions r0,r1 under the next variable are constants or residuals at level i+1. Realize r=(not x_{i+1} AND r0) OR (x_{i+1} AND r1), using at most two AND gates and one OR gate; share one NOT gate per input variable. Build from level q-1 upward. Induction on q-i shows each node computes its residual, so the root computes h. There are at most qw residual nodes and q shared NOT gates, hence at most 3qw+q gates. In particular, q may be superlogarithmic in a parameter s while the compilation remains polynomial in s if q(s)w(s) is polynomial in s. The hypothesis is a residual-width condition; no such bound is established here for MMW19's oracle predicates.

Each term uses at most q-1 AND gates, the OR uses at most 2^q-1 gates, and at most q NOT gates provide negative literals. Constants handle empty or full accepting sets. This costs at most 2^q(q+1)+1 gates per replacement. Substitute each replacement and retain the B other gates; fan-out adds wires but no gates. evidence: The DNF construction is correct: any Boolean function h on q variables has a DNF with at most 2^q terms (one per accepting input). statement: Bounded-query truth-table compilation lemma. Let C be a Boolean circuit with g oracle gates, where gate i computes an arbitrary Boolean function f_i on q_i input bits. Replacing each oracle gate by an oracle-free fan-in-2 circuit computing the same function increases the total gate count by at most O(sum_{i=1}^g q_i 2^{q_i}). In particular, if every q_i <= a log_2 s + b for fixed constants a,b and g <= s^d for a fixed d, then the replacement overhead is polynomial in s. Proof: For each f_i, write its truth table as a disjunction of the at most 2^{q_i} input minterms on which it equals 1. Each minterm uses O(q_i) fan-in-2 gates, and combining the minterms uses O(2^{q_i}) gates. Thus gate i costs O(q_i 2^{q_i}); summing gives the stated overhead. If q_i <= a log_2 s+b, then 2^{q_i} <= 2^b s^a, so the sum is O(g (log s) s^a), polynomial when g <= s^d. The construction preserves the circuit’s Boolean function because each replacement computes exactly f_i on every possible input.

statement_start: LEMMA (Exact Simulation Overhead for Oracle-Query Compilation). Let M be any one-pass streaming algorithm for Search-MCSP[s] that uses an oracle O. Suppose M makes at most g oracle queries on inputs of stream length N, and each query has bit-length at most q. Consider the standard compilation that replaces each oracle gate by a Boolean circuit computing the exact same function f: {0,1}^q -> {0,1} via its full truth table (i.e., a DNF/CNF of size O(q * 2^q) or a binary decision tree of size O(2^q)). Then the resulting oracle-free circuit has size at most O(g * q * 2^q). This compilation is polynomial in the stream parameter s if and only if q = O(log s). Proof: (1) A Boolean function on q bits has a truth table of 2^q entries. The standard circuit constructions (DNF, CNF, or binary decision tree) yield size O(q * 2^q) = O(2^{q + log q}). (2) With g queries, total overhead is O(g * q * 2^q). (3) For this to be poly(s), we need q * 2^q = poly(s). Taking logs: q + log q = O(log s), which holds iff q = O(log s). (4) Conversely, if q = O(log s), then 2^q = poly(s) and the compilation is poly(s). (5) Therefore, the Transfer T0 --- which requires a poly(s) simulation to apply Theorem 4.1 (the streaming-to-circuit connection) --- succeeds exactly when the oracle query length satisfies q = O(log s), and fails (i.e., the compilation is superpolynomial) exactly when q = omega(log s). This lemma makes no claim about the intrinsic complexity of the oracle function (e.g., Sigma3SAT^A); it is a statement about the cost of *this specific compilation method*.

statement: One-hot realization lemma. Let Q be a finite state set of size M, let Σ be a finite input alphabet, and let δ_t:Q×Σ→Q be any deterministic (possibly time-dependent) transition function at update t. For each a∈Σ define the M×M matrix A_{t,a} by (A_{t,a})_{r,q}=1 iff δ_t(q,a)=r. Then for every q∈Q, A_{t,a}e_q=e_{δ_t(q,a)}. If F⊆Q is the accepting set, the row vector f_F with (f_F)_q=1 iff q∈F satisfies f_Fe_q=1 iff q∈F. Thus every such finite-state streaming computation has an exact linear realization in dimension M under one-hot state encoding. Proof: the q-th column of A_{t,a} has exactly one 1, in row δ_t(q,a); multiplying by e_q selects that column. The decoder statement follows from the definition of f_F. This gives no polynomial-dimension bound in the state-bit parameter S=ceil(log2 M): M may equal 2^S, and it does not establish the (R),(L),(E) hypotheses or treewidth bound required by T0.

proved_step: statement: Candidate lemma: Let X be a finite set of truth tables and let A subset X be the yes instances. Suppose a deterministic decoder D of the final state q(x) outputs none for x outside A and outputs a circuit C with Eval(C)=x for every x in A. Then q is injective on X. Proof: if x != y and q(x)=q(y), D returns the same output on both. If exactly one is in A, the output must be both none and a circuit. If both are in A, the same circuit would evaluate to both x and y, contradiction. Thus no distinct pair collides.
